hero.title: Product-Quality Assurance & Authenticity Confidence for Category Trial
hero.tagline: Removes the single largest behavioral barrier — fear of receiving counterfeit, expired, or sub-standard products — that prevents existing Zepto customers from trying non-grocery categories.

whyThisWon.businessValue: Unlocking these categories directly expands Zepto's total addressable market per customer. Beauty and personal care alone is a $28B Indian market growing 39% YoY online. This is a growth play, not a defensive play.
whyThisWon.userValue: It removes the single largest behavioral barrier — fear of receiving counterfeit, expired, or sub-standard products — that prevents existing Zepto customers from trying non-grocery categories. The concern appears across beauty, personal care, supplements, baby care, pet care, and premium packaged goods.
whyThisWon.behaviouralReasoning: High-involvement items evoke acute Loss Aversion and Perceived Risk (Kahneman & Tversky, 1979). Explicit assurances lower risk perception in unfamiliar categories (Bauer, 1960); prominent quality seals credibly signal platform integrity (Spence, 1973); structural assurances drive initial purchase intention (McKnight et al., 2002).

comparisonTradeOffs.opp_quality_assurance: Wins on every weighted dimension — the strongest triangulation across evidence, theory, industry, and academic support.
comparisonTradeOffs.opp_support_refund: Defensive intervention — addresses what happens after a bad experience; business value is limited to churn reduction rather than new revenue.
comparisonTradeOffs.opp_fulfillment_control: Fatal weakness is implementation complexity — real-time substitution requires dark-store integration that would consume the entire graduation timeline.
comparisonTradeOffs.opp_freshness_guarantee: Narrow category scope (fresh produce, dairy, meat only); many trust mechanisms overlap with the primary MVP.
comparisonTradeOffs.opp_category_onboarding: Weakest evidence base (14 records); downstream of the trust problem — customers first need to trust product quality.

assumptions: Category trial is primarily blocked by trust, not price or awareness. This assumption is supported by the evidence base (27 records citing quality/authenticity concerns vs. minimal price-related friction in non-grocery categories).
Visual trust badges measurably reduce perceived risk. Supported by Signaling Theory (Spence, 1973) and Initial Trust Formation Model (McKnight et al., 2002). Requires A/B validation.

Existing Zepto grocery customers are the target audience for category expansion. The evidence base primarily captures existing users expressing hesitation about specific categories, not first-time platform adopters.
Zepto has (or can establish) supply-chain controls to back authenticity claims for non-grocery categories. This requires commercial agreements with brand partners.
Post-delivery resolution can be handled within existing OMS. The MVP assumes Zepto's order management system supports instant refund/replacement for quality issues without manual intervention.
The 10-minute delivery promise is not undermined by adding quality assurance steps. The intervention is UX-level; it does not change picking or delivery workflows.

outlook.expectedUserOutcome: First-time trial of high-involvement categories becomes friction-free: category-shelf assurance and product provenance reduce perceived risk, and a single-tap resolution entrypoint protects buyers after delivery.
outlook.expectedBusinessOutcome: Expands total addressable market per customer by unlocking high-margin non-grocery categories (beauty, personal care, baby care, wellness); measured by the percentage of Monthly Active Customers purchasing from at least one lifetime-new category per month.
outlook.primaryMetric: Percentage of Monthly Active Customers purchasing from at least one lifetime-new category per month.
outlook.guardrailMetric: Post-delivery refund/issue request rate must remain < 3%.

risks.risk: Brands refuse to be listed alongside an authenticity badge without formal partnership
risks.mitigation: Start with first-party / Zepto-sourced inventory; expand to third-party with commercial agreements

risks.risk: Refund abuse through the "instant resolution" entrypoint
risks.mitigation: Implement abuse detection; cap resolution frequency per customer; require photo evidence

risks.risk: Quality assurance badges do not move the category trial metric
risks.mitigation: A/B test badge variants before full rollout; measure pre/post category conversion

risks.risk: Operational data (batch origins, expiry windows) is not available in the current dark-store system
risks.mitigation: Limit initial scope to categories where data is available; add manual override for data-gap items

risks.risk: Existing customers do not perceive non-grocery categories as relevant to their needs
risks.mitigation: Combine with targeted category discovery; address awareness alongside trust
